transcript.content: Good [morning/afternoon], thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because my eating has gotten kind of out of hand. Like after my cashier shifts, I’ll be tired and I’ll stop for takeout, and it turns into these huge orders—burgers, fries, chicken, desserts, like enough for a whole family.

And then I just sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I go home. I don’t know, it sounds bad saying it out loud. My job is right near a bunch of fast food places too, which doesn’t help, and after standing there all day dealing with people and the register beeping nonstop… I don’t know, I just end up doing it.
After these large eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising a lot, or skipping meals?

Um… I don’t know, not really sure how to answer that exactly. Like, I feel really guilty after, and I’ll tell myself I need to “fix it” somehow, but then my schedule is all weird with cashier shifts and sometimes I’m just running late or whatever.

I haven’t really thought of it as, like, a plan to undo it. Mostly I just feel bad and try not to think about it, honestly.
When you're eating these large amounts of food, do you feel like you can't stop yourself or control how much you're eating?

Yeah… yeah, that’s pretty much it. Like, once I take that first bite, it’s like something in me clicks off. I’ll be sitting there telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but my hands just keep reaching for the next thing anyway.

And it’s weird because I’m not even always enjoying it the whole time. Like sometimes I’m thinking about the bus schedule or how this one customer yelled at me over a coupon earlier, and then I look down and half the food’s gone. So… yeah, it feels like I can’t really stop it once it starts.
Do you often eat so quickly during these episodes that you don’t really realize how much you’ve eaten until you’re uncomfortably full?

Yeah… yeah, that happens a lot. I’ll be eating fast, like I’m just trying to get through it, and then all of a sudden I realize I’ve gone way past full.

A lot of nights my stomach gets so tight it actually hurts, and I’ll have to lean the car seat back if I’m still out there, or when I get home I just lie in bed really still and wait for it to pass. It’s embarrassing. Sometimes I’m just staring at my phone or thinking about something dumb from work, like whether the drawer was off or whatever, and then I look down and it’s like… oh, I ate all that.
How often do these episodes happen—like, how many times a week or month would you say you experience this kind of eating where you feel out of control?

Um… lately, I guess it’s been like three or four nights most weeks. Sometimes I try to tell myself it wasn’t that many, because one week blends into the next, you know, especially when I’m closing at the store and then opening again, and I’m tired and eating in the car or whatever.

But if I’m being honest… since those foreclosure calls started, I don’t think there’s been a single week where it didn’t happen at least once. It’s embarrassing to say that out loud.
Do these eating episodes make it hard for you to function normally, like affecting your work, relationships, or how you feel about yourself?

Yeah… I mean, I still go to work. I don’t really miss my cashier shifts or anything, because bills don’t care how you feel, you know? And my manager already acts like the schedule is some kind of sacred thing—he posts it late and then gets mad when people can’t cover, which is a whole other mess.

But… it’s more at home, I guess. I’m spending money we really don’t have on food, and then I’m hiding it from my wife. Like I’ll throw away bags before I get inside, or I’ll act like the card charge was for gas or something. And then I’m walking around the apartment feeling like I’m lying just by standing there.

So yeah, I function, technically, but home feels tense. Like I’m keeping secrets, and I hate that.
Do you feel a lot of shame or distress about these eating episodes, even when they aren’t affecting your work or home life directly?

Yeah… shame is probably the main thing, honestly. Even if nobody’s saying anything to me, I feel disgusting about it.

That’s why I hide it. I’ll eat in the parking lot sometimes, just sitting there in the car like I’m doing something normal, but I’m really hoping nobody I know walks by. Or I’ll wait until my wife is asleep and then eat, and afterward I’m trying to shove the bags and receipts way down in the trash so she won’t see how much I had.

And then the next morning I’m acting normal, like I didn’t just do this whole secret thing. It’s… yeah, it’s humiliating.
Do you often eat so fast or in secret because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… I do. I mean, the secret part for sure. I’ll hide it because I’m ashamed, like I don’t want anyone seeing the amount.

Sometimes I’ll just sit in the parking lot and eat before I even go home, which is stupid because people are walking by with their carts and I’m trying to act casual, like I’m just checking my phone or something. Or if I do bring stuff home, I’ll wait until my wife is asleep. Then afterward I’m stuffing the bags and receipts down in the trash so she won’t see how much I had.

It’s not even just the food, it’s all the covering it up. That’s the part that makes me feel really low.
When you think about these eating episodes, is your main concern about how it affects your weight or body shape, or is it more about how it makes you feel about yourself as a person?

I don’t know… I guess it’s hard to separate those. Like, I do think about weight sometimes, sure, but when it happens it’s more like… I just feel like I’m failing at being a normal person.

Not to sound dramatic. It’s just, I’ll be sitting there afterward thinking, “Why did I do that again?” And then I start thinking about stupid stuff, like how at work people will return a candy bar because they grabbed the wrong kind, and I’m like, I couldn’t even stop myself from buying a whole bag of things I didn’t need. Which isn’t really the same thing, I know.

So… yeah, I’m not sure if I can answer it cleanly. It’s more about how I feel about myself, I think.
Do you find that these eating episodes cause you significant emotional distress or interfere with your daily life, even aside from the guilt or shame you feel afterward?

Yeah… I mean, I still make it to work. I’m not missing my cashier shifts or anything like that, so part of me wants to say it’s not interfering, but… it is, just in a quieter way.

Like, I’m spending money we really don’t have on food. And then I’m trying to cover that up too, which turns into this whole other thing. I’ll be checking the bank app and thinking, okay, maybe she won’t notice that charge, or maybe it just looks like gas station stuff… which sounds ridiculous when I say it.

And at home it just makes everything feel tense. Not because she’s doing anything wrong, but because I’m walking around with all these little secrets. So even if I show up to work and pay the bills mostly on time, it still feels like I’m making home dishonest, if that makes sense.
